idiom_name: public wrapper functions taking pthread_mutex_lock + static *_locked helpers
implementation_notes: ISO C offers no visibility rules beyond translation units and no ownership assertions, so the discipline is a convention: a public function locks the component's mutex, calls a static helper named *_locked that works on the state directly, and unlocks on every path. POSIX makes the constraint concrete - with a PTHREAD_MUTEX_NORMAL or PTHREAD_MUTEX_DEFAULT mutex an attempted relock deadlocks, so the helper must never lock; PTHREAD_MUTEX_ERRORCHECK returns EDEADLK instead, which makes it the debug aid for catching an accidental relock, while PTHREAD_MUTEX_RECURSIVE is the workaround POSIX itself warns about around condition variables. Giving the helpers internal linkage (static) is what keeps the precondition inside the translation unit.
pitfalls: Helpers must have internal linkage (static); an exported *_locked function invites callers that do not hold the mutex and turns the precondition into a data race.
pthread_mutex_lock can fail: with PTHREAD_MUTEX_ERRORCHECK a relock returns EDEADLK, and unlocking unconditionally afterwards is wrong.
The recursive-mutex workaround is not free - POSIX notes that an implicit unlock during pthread_cond_wait may not release a mutex locked more than once, and relocks silently inflate the lock count.
Nothing checks the precondition at runtime; an ownership assertion (record pthread_self in the struct) or a debug-only ERRORCHECK mutex is the only feedback.
